Teaching a Neural Network to play 2048 (+ cat)

This document uses special characters like the em-dash (—). These characters were lovingly hand-inserted and not a result of AI-generated text.

Okay, this is my first ever blog post. This may suck. I'm sorry in advance.

TL;DR: I made an AI that plays 2048

I've been mildly (okay, extremely) obsessed with 2048 since I was around ten years old. Something about the funny tiles with big numbers tickles my brain really good. Anyways, I'm studying computer science in college right now, and lately I've gotten interested in learning about machine learning. So I figured, why not combine the two?

Plot Twist: I don't know what I'm doing

I got all hyped up about making a 2048 bot, but soon got brought back to the crushing reality that: I'm a stupid little undergrad with a smooth little brain and do not know much about machine learning.

I started looking into some machine learning techniques, and the one that stood out to me most was imitation learning — basically, monkey see, monkey do. The reason? I honestly just wanted to avoid the headache of coming up with a way to "quantify" or "rank" how good a move is. With imitation learning, each state-action pair is directly labeled, and the model just learns to do the same.

What would I do? Let’s make the bot guess

Thanks to doing some undergrad research assistant stuff under my researchman (if you're reading this shahab or guven, hi!!! you guys are super cool, thanks for putting up with me lmao), I know that usually training these types of models requires massive amounts of data. Like, tens or even hundreds of thousands of games. So of course, my first instinct is to search online for some pre-existing datasets I can use.

I did manage to find some datasets of 2048 games online, but after digging into the stats, it turns out those players don’t perform nearly as well as I do.

I've been mildly (okay, extremely) obsessed with 2048 since I was around ten, and my highscore pictured below, speaks for itself. Simply put, I am very good at this game. The existing datasets don’t reflect that level of play, and frankly, they fall short compared to my own. If I want my model to do well, it should learn from the best (me). Therefore, I think the models will do well if it imitates my play style.
  • while reading up online, the first "method" i came across was using multilayer perceptrons.
  • i tried the method, it didn't work super well, but it was my first model so i was still pretty excited
  • i realized, if someone wanted to try playing some games then switching in the bot mid-way, or sometimes just during gameplay the sides will swap/rotate, so i added in 8 rotations
  • i find out about cnn's, i think they make more i sense, i try them out, it works much much better!!!
  • i try doing rl with self-play and ... it gets dumber. what :D put on backburner for now
  • main issue abt my cnn is it dies a lot early game, but if it somehow survives the earlygame, it does well, i think is because of rotation noise, so try removing earlygame in all rotations
  • it also does moves i am forced to do when it's not forced to, so i deleted all data of me choosing the down key
  • this somehow made my model even worse, so back to the drawing board!
  • i realize my model may be overfitting, so i add dropout layers
